meta.title: Birth Doula Certification
meta.description: ADA Birth Doula certification: culturally integrated training for labor and delivery support, cohorts on a rolling basis, and a written and practical exam.

courseDescription: Culturally integrated training and certification for labor and delivery support.

hero.line: Cohorts run on a rolling basis throughout the year.

steps.title: How to get certified
steps.intro: A birth doula gives families continuous physical, emotional and informational support through labor and delivery, from early labor to the immediate postpartum period. Four steps take you from an ADA cohort to a public record in the ADA registry.

s1.title: Join an ADA Birth Doula cohort
s1.body: Cohorts run on a rolling basis throughout the year. No prior experience is required. Contact us for upcoming start dates and current cohort pricing. <link>Find an ADA course</link>

s2.title: Complete the Birth Doula Program
s2.body: {count} topics, from the stages of labor to immediate postpartum support.

s3.title: Sit the ADA Birth Doula exam
s3.bodyNext: A written and a practical exam. The next Birth Doula exam is on <d>{date}</d>. <link>Exam dates</link>
s3.bodyNone: A written and a practical exam.

s4.title: Join the registry, then renew
s4.body: ADA issues your certificate, numbered in the form {format}, and lists you in the ADA registry. Certification is valid for {validity}. Check the registry

topics.title: What the program covers
topics.intro: The Birth Doula Program brings the same culturally integrated approach as the postpartum program: traditional Asian birthing practices with modern evidence-based care, delivered in the family’s preferred language.
topics.imageAlt: An instructor teaches a session of an ADA program, with a slide on a wall screen
topics.caption: An instructor teaches a session of the ADA Postpartum Doula Program. {date}.

items.stages: Stages of labor and physiological birth

cohorts.label: Cohorts
cohorts.value: On a rolling basis, throughout the year.

prerequisites.label: Prerequisites
prerequisites.value: None. You need no prior experience, and you do not need to be a Postpartum Doula first.

tuition.label: Tuition
tuition.value: Contact us for current cohort pricing, scholarship availability and payment options. <link>Scholarships</link>

compare.title: How it differs from Postpartum Doula
compare.intro: Birth Doula is an independent certification track. You can pursue it on its own, and you can hold both credentials.
compare.caption: ADA Birth Doula compared with ADA Postpartum Doula

cta.title: Ask about the next Birth Doula cohort.

next.q: When is the next Birth Doula cohort?
next.a: Cohorts run on a rolling basis throughout the year. Write to us to be added to the next cohort’s enrollment list, and we will share the upcoming start dates.

languages.q: Is the program available in more than one language?
languages.a: Yes. As with the Postpartum Doula track, training and exams are offered in {languages}.

postpartumFirst.q: Do I need to be a Postpartum Doula first?
postpartumFirst.a: No. Birth Doula is an independent certification track and can be pursued on its own.
